newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index ends on rally after year's low.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index ends on rally after year's low.

text.p: Shenzhen's B shares closed on a powerful rebound on Thursday after hitting a low for the year on Wednesday, and analysts said they expected to see more gains on Friday led by stocks likely to post good 1997 interim results.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index shot up 5.16 points or 4.28 percent to 125.59 points on turnover of HK$95 million compared with HK$94 million on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, it closed at its year-low at 120.44 points.
The A share index lost 7.1 points or 1.83 percent to 380.33 due in part to selling in market leader Shenzhen Development Bank Co just ahead of the close, brokers said.
Turnover in the A share market was 4.4 billion yuan against Wednesday's 4.7 billion yuan.
"I think the B index's sharp rise is largely technical," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"The average B share P/E (price earnings ratio) has dropped from 14 times to about 11 times after the recent plunges, while Shanghai's B share P/E has stayed at around 15 times," she said.
"So there is still room for the Shenzhen B market to rise," she added.
Some analysts said they expected the rally to extend, albeit less aggressively than on Thursday, on companies expected to post healthy interim results by the August 30 deadline.
"The B index rose on a strong rebound staged by stocks expected to post good interim results," another Guotai analyst said.
Guangdong Electric Power Development Co Ltd, which analysts said could be among those that did well, was among the best B share performers and rose HK$0.50 to HK$5.60.
"The market still has upward strength," an analyst at Hainan Provincial Trust and Investment Co said.
"This may be a bear-trap," a J&A Securities (HK) analyst warned. "This does not look like the beginning of a bull-run because turnover is not heavy enough."

The market mood turned sour when the July 1 handover of Hong Kong from British to Chinese rule failed to improve sentiment, as many investors had expected the historic event to inspire buying interest.
In the A share market, leading counter Shenzhen Development Bank dropped 0.92 yuan or 2.86 percent to 33.08 yuan on volume of 7.86 million shares.
